title: Complex Magnetic Phases and Unconventional Skyrmion Thermodynamics in Magnetically Intercalated Cr$_{1+x}$Te$_2$Compounds
authors: Clayton Conner, Santosh Karki Chhetri, Avinash Sah, Manoj Gadtoula, Dilan M. Gamachchi, Indeewari M. Karunarathne, Steven Kelley, Andrew C. Meng, Jacob Cook, Cheng Zhang, Jin Hu, Yue Li, Hoyeon Jeon, An-Ping Li, Zheng Gai, Guang Bian
abstract: Chemical intercalation provides a powerful route for tuning the electronic and magnetic properties of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), enabling the emergence of magnetic phases and phenomena that are otherwise inaccessible in their pristine forms. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of magnetically intercalated Cr$_{1+x}$Te$_2$ through a combination of scanning tunneling microscopy, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, magnetization, electrical transport, and Lorentz transmission electron microscopy measurements. We uncover a rich magnetic phase diagram comprising paramagnetic, in-plane spin-fluctuation, out-of-plane ferromagnetic, and field-induced Néel-type skyrmion phases. In particular, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy directly reveals the formation of Néel-type skyrmion textures slightly below the Curie temperature, with their configurations evolving strongly with temperature and magnetic field. The skyrmions exhibit pronounced thermal hysteresis and coexist with stripe domains, indicative of a complex magnetic energy landscape arising from the competition among disorder-induced local Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, and dipolar interactions. Our results demonstrate that chemical intercalation can profoundly reshape the magnetic interactions and phase behavior of TMDs, establishing Cr$_{1+x}$Te$_2$ as a versatile platform for exploring tunable magnetism, skyrmion physics, and unconventional thermodynamic phenomena in low-dimensional quantum materials.
summary: This work explores the tunable magnetism and skyrmion physics in intercalated $	ext{Cr}_{1+x}	ext{Te}_2$. By combining multiple advanced measurements, the researchers map out a complex magnetic phase diagram featuring Néel-type skyrmions. The findings demonstrate that chemical intercalation allows precise control over the magnetic interactions, making the material a versatile model for studying unconventional magnetic thermodynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex magnetic phases and unconventional thermodynamics associated with skyrmion formation in magnetically intercalated $	ext{Cr}_{1+x}	ext{Te}_2$ compounds.
main_result: The material exhibits a rich magnetic phase diagram, transitioning through paramagnetic, spin-fluctuation, and field-induced Néel-type skyrmion phases, governed by competing magnetic interactions.
method: The research employs a combination of advanced experimental techniques, including STM, ARPES, magnetization measurements, electrical transport, and crucially, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (LTEM).
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Cr}_{1+x}	ext{Te}_2$, a transition metal dichalcogenide whose magnetic properties are tuned by chemical intercalation. The magnetism is governed by a complex energy landscape arising from the competition between perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, dipolar interactions, and disorder-induced chiral interactions.
key_observables: Magnetic phase diagram (Paramagnetic $ightarrow$ IPSF $ightarrow$ Skyrmion $ightarrow$ FM), skyrmion size and density, magnetization ($M(H), M(T)$), and AC magnetic susceptibility ($\chi'$ and $\chi''$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), applied magnetic field ($H$), and the degree of intercalation disorder ($x$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that local symmetry breaking due to $	ext{Cr}$-site disorder is the source of chiral interactions stabilizing the skyrmions, despite the average crystal structure being centrosymmetric.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, electronic band structure (ARPES), magnetic transitions ($M(T)$), and directly image the temperature and field dependence of Néel-type skyrmion textures using LTEM.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes the structure and electronic properties, maps out the magnetic phase diagram using bulk measurements, and finally uses LTEM to visualize and analyze the temperature and field evolution of the skyrmion phases.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete, tunable platform for observing complex, non-equilibrium magnetic textures (skyrmions) whose thermodynamics are dictated by the competition between various long-range and local interactions, which is highly relevant to many-body physics and phase transitions.
